subject: Next steps: model fit benchmarks + callable JSON schema validation for Cobalt Analytics
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: model fit benchmarks + callable JSON schema validation for Cobalt Analytics

Hi Tariq —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposal so we have alignment before we spin up the evaluation:

What we heard from you:
- Primary use: structured extraction from clinical notes + enrichment for analytics dashboards.
- Success metrics: >92% schema-complete responses for target fields, latency <350ms p50 on live traffic, and predictable token cost.
- Constraints: PHI sensitivity, need for SOC2 evidence, and a short pilot timeline (2 weeks).

Redwood recommended evaluation plan (48–72 hour run):
1) Models to benchmark (suggested):
   - Mistral-Instruct-30B (float16 quantized path) — good for high-quality instruction-following on long context.
   - Llama-2-13b-chat (int8) — lower cost baseline with robust JSON output when combined with schema constraints.
   - RedMulch-7B-chat (4-bit quantized) — cost-optimized candidate for high-throughput endpoints.

2) What we’ll measure: schema completeness, field-level exact match / normalized match, hallucination rate (unexpected keys/values), average tokens per response, and end-to-end latency.

3) Structured output approach:
   - We’ll enforce a JSON schema at generation time using a callable validation step (function \"validate_payload\") that runs in the inference pipeline and triggers up to 3 retry attempts with exponential backoff if the payload fails validation.
   - Retry policy: 3 retries, jittered backoff (200ms -> 500ms -> 1200ms), max cumulative additional latency budget 1.5s. Retries will attempt diverse decoding (top_p/temp variations) to avoid deterministic failures.

4) Data & logistics:
   - Please share a small sample set (~250 rows) of redacted notes and an example expected output for 10 records.
   - We’ll need SSH/SAML provisioning for your staging environment or a secure upload to the Drive link below.

Attached is a short benchmark plan and the schema proposal we’d like you to review.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a kickoff for next Tuesday (Mar 9) to provision the endpoints and hand over the test harness to your team.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
[Attachment: cobalt-benchmarks-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

Monica — really appreciate the recap and clear plan. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit the sample dataset: 

- SOC2/data residency: Procurement needs a short list of SOC2 artifacts and confirmation of where logs/keys will live during the pilot. Can you send the SOC2 poster or a short evidence checklist?
- Pilot cost: procurement asked for an order-of-magnitude estimate for the 48–72 hour benchmark (token estimate or flat pilot fee). Could you provide a rough number or range?
- Schema question: for address and provider fields, is your validation tolerant of nulls vs empty strings? We prefer explicit nulls for missing data.

I’m looping in procurement to keep the contract folks in the loop. We can share a redacted sample by end of day Friday. Also happy to join the kickoff on Mar 9.

Best,
Tariq Rahman
Head of Product, Cobalt Analytics

Tariq —

Quick answers from the infra/SE side:
- SOC2 & evidence: I attached a one-page SOC2 checklist with what we can share for a pilot (scope, logs, retentions). Full reports require an NDA + enterprise request but pilot evidence (syslogs, endpoint audit traces) is available.
- Pilot cost estimate: for a 72-hour run with mixed read/write traffic (~50k tokens/day synthetic + 200 concurrent short calls), rough estimate is $1,800–$3,200 depending on model mix (we’ll provide a token-level breakdown post-run). We can also quote a flat pilot fee if you prefer procurement simplicity.
- Null handling: our validation will accept explicit nulls. The schema-proposal.json included sets \"nullable\": true for optional fields and will normalize empty-string -> null when configured.

Proposed technical kickoff & test plan (high level):
1) Day 0 (provisioning): grant staging access, upload sample corpus to Drive.
2) Day 1 (warm-up): run small-scale sanities, tune decoding params for schema-hit rate.
3) Day 2 (full run): benchmark three model candidates, collect token-level telemetry, and run schema-compliance sweep with our validate_payload hook.
4) Delivery: we’ll share a report (benchmarks PDF) + a baseline regression test set and suggested guardrail config (retries, decode presets).

Links & artifacts:
- Schema proposal (attached): schema-proposal.json
- Test harness (private GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/cobalt-pilot-harness
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/COB-2027-042
